answer: An agent marketplace coordinating harbor shipments of velvet and ferrous scrap requires each bidding identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can compete for jobs. Creating accounts is cheap, but activating 10,000 fake agents ties up $1 million for a month. The lock prevents an attacker from recycling the same funds through fresh identities, making a sybil swarm consume capital in proportion to its size.
